title: Chirp Instrument
hook: Play the last fifth of a second of two black holes.
sub: Real LIGO strain from GW150914, tracked half-wave by half-wave into MIDI. A quantum blur on a simulated 20-qubit register then scatters it. Tap through it, scrub the blur, loop the merger, and jam over it.
you_control: Tap the black holes in the scene (or the pad, or Z/X): each tap sends out one real half-wave, and you watch it land on the two LIGO observatories (light runs down their arms, one arm stretches as the other squeezes), or press Play
Scrub the quantum blur's reach (off, 0, 0.5) and watch its cloud of real notes spread; mute the H1/L1 voices by tapping the observatories
Loop any stretch by dragging the tape under the scene (or the roll in Data), or pick Inspiral / Merger
Jam on the keyboard over the loop (on-screen or A-;)
qubits_note: qubits=20 is the engine's maximum budget per pass, and the cached job records show qubits=20 and resolution=2 were sent. Each GW150914 track's piano roll is 42 pitch rows x ~11.6k steps (resolution 2 ticks), which needs ceil(log2 42)+ceil(log2 11633) = 6+14 = 20 qubits by the Quantum Blur grid rule. That is our calculation; the engine does not report its width. The reach-0.5 output span of MIDI 41-82 (42 rows) matches it.
honesty: A classical sonification of public LIGO data (CC BY 4.0). Only the blur is quantum, and it was simulated on Atlas, not run on hardware. GW170817's pitch is model-guided and it has no blur.
